abstract: |
  Using k-means clustering to estimate behavioural states from high-frequency 3D GPS-tracking data. Here we use instantaneous flight variables (rate of ascent/descent, speed, and absolute turn angles) to classify the behavioural states of wedge-tailed eagles. This is a subset of the same variables used by @Bergen2022-rj.

# Load packages

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("psych", "cluster", "leaflet")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

```

# Import data

```{r}

load(file = "data/eagledata4.Rdata")
unique(eagledata4$age)

eagledata4 <- eagledata4 %>% ungroup()

head(eagledata4, 10)

```

## How many locations does each individual have?

```{r}

eagledata4 %>% 
  group_by(name) %>%
  summarize(n = n(),
            Mindate = format(min(date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
            Maxdate = format(max(date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
            Mindatetime = min(stepend_dtime),
            Maxdatetime = max(stepend_dtime))

```

# Select a subset of the data for prototyping

To reduce the dataset while testing models, we'll use a single eagle's data.

```{r}

# to use all data
# which_data <- "all"

# to pick a single eagle's data
# which_data <- "Stella"
which_data <- "Tabatha"

if(which_data == "all") {
  # keep all data
  eagle_data <- eagledata4
  } else {
    # filter to the single eagle
    eagle_data <- eagledata4 %>% filter(name == which_data)
  }

```

### Flight information

How many flight segments, and how many locations in each?

```{r}

# check number of unique segments
length(unique(eagle_data$flight_n)) 

# how many locations in each flight segment?
segment_lengths <- eagle_data %>% 
  group_by(flight_n) %>% 
  summarize(len = n())

segment_lengths %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = len), bins = 100) +
  labs(title = "Number of locations per flight segment",
       x = "Number of locations per flight segment",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_bw()

segment_lengths %>% 
  ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = len), bins = 100) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Number of locations per flight segment (log)",
       x = "Number of locations per flight segment",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_bw()

```

## Create features for clustering

```{r}

eagle_data <- eagle_data %>% rename(F_Vrate_abs = F_absVrate)

eagle_data <- eagle_data %>% 
  mutate(
    F_radians = step_ta,                  # step_ta was already in radians
    F_radians_abs = abs(F_radians),       # make radian absolute value
    F_AOG = ifelse(F_AOG < 0 ,0, F_AOG),  # make all negative AOG values 0
    .after = F_Vrate_abs
   )

head(eagle_data, 10)

```

```{r}

ggplot(data = eagle_data) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(x = F_Sn),
                 bins = 100, fill = "skyblue", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 2)) +
  theme_bw()

eagle_data <- eagle_data %>% filter(F_Sn >= 1)

ggplot(data = eagle_data) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(x = F_Sn),
                 bins = 100, fill = "skyblue", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 2)) +
  theme_bw()

```

# Data explorer

We want to visually assess the flight paths with respect to the flight variables.

A single flight segment is plotted over a satellite basemap. Hover over a location to see the values of all flight variables at that fix, and use the *Colour by* dropdown (top right) to colour the locations by each variable (the white flight path line can be toggled off). The aim is to see which variables clearly separate the visually identifiable states, such as thermalling (tight circles with positive vertical rate) and flapping/directional flight (straight lines).

The colour scales are clipped to the 1st–99th percentiles of each variable so that a few extreme values don't wash out the colours (the hover values are unclipped). Variables that take both negative and positive values (`F_Vrate` and `F_radians`) use a diverging palette centred on 0 (red = positive, blue = negative).

```{r}

# the variables plotted in the previous chunks
explore_vars <- c("F_AOG", "F_radians", "F_speed", "F_Sn", "F_Vrate", "F_Vrate_abs", "F_radians_abs")

# variables with negative and positive values get a diverging palette centred on 0
diverging_vars <- c("F_radians", "F_Vrate")

# written as a function so it can be re-used later, e.g. with the k-means
# behaviour labels: flight_explorer(segment_to_plot, c("behavior", explore_vars))
flight_explorer <- function(segment, vars, diverging = character(0), height = 650) {

  segment <- segment %>% arrange(stepend_dtime)
  n_fix <- nrow(segment)

  # hover labels - timestamp and the (unclipped) value of every variable
  label_rows <- map(vars, \(v) {
    val <- segment[[v]]
    val <- if (is.numeric(val)) as.character(round(val, 3)) else as.character(val)
    paste0("<tr><td>", v, "</td>",
           "<td style='text-align:right; padding-left:10px;'><b>", val, "</b></td></tr>")
  })
  labels <- paste0("<b>", format(segment$stepend_dtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "</b>",
                   " (fix ", seq_len(n_fix), " of ", n_fix, ")",
                   "<table>", reduce(label_rows, paste0), "</table>") %>%
    map(htmltools::HTML)

  # colour palette for each variable
  make_palette <- function(x, v) {
    if (!is.numeric(x)) {
      okabe_ito <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
                     "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999")
      x <- factor(x)
      pal <- colorFactor(okabe_ito[seq_along(levels(x))], domain = x)
      return(list(pal = pal, x = x))
    }
    lims <- quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    if (v %in% diverging) {
      lims <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(lims))
      pal <- colorNumeric("RdBu", domain = lims, reverse = TRUE)
    } else {
      pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = lims)
    }
    list(pal = pal, x = pmin(pmax(x, lims[1]), lims[2])) # clip to the colour range
  }

  palettes <- map(set_names(vars), \(v) make_palette(segment[[v]], v))
  # the point colours for each variable (switched in the browser by the dropdown)
  point_colours <- map(palettes, \(p) p$pal(p$x))

  # a single layer of points (so the hover labels aren't duplicated for every variable)
  m <- leaflet(segment, height = height, width = "100%",
               options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
    addPolylines(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, color = "white", weight = 1,
                 opacity = 0.6, group = "Flight path") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE,
                     fillColor = point_colours[[1]], fillOpacity = 0.9,
                     layerId = paste0("fix", seq_len(n_fix)), label = labels,
                     labelOptions = labelOptions(textsize = "12px", direction = "auto"))

  # one legend per variable - only the selected one is shown
  for (v in vars) {
    m <- m %>%
      addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = palettes[[v]]$pal, values = palettes[[v]]$x,
                title = v, opacity = 1, className = paste0("info legend legend-var legend-", v))
  }

  m %>%
    addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Flight path",
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
    addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>%
    # add a 'Colour by' dropdown that recolours the points and switches the legend
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var map = this;
        function colourBy(v) {
          var cols = data.cols[v];
          for (var i = 1; i <= data.n; i++) {
            var m = map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix' + i);
            if (m) m.setStyle({fillColor: cols[i - 1]});
          }
          el.querySelectorAll('.legend-var').forEach(function(l) {
            l.style.display = l.classList.contains('legend-' + v) ? '' : 'none';
          });
        }
        // leaflet only draws the layers once the map is visible (e.g. inside
        // a tab), so wait until the points exist before adding the dropdown
        function setup() {
          if (!map.layerManager || !map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix1')) {
            setTimeout(setup, 200);
            return;
          }
          addDropdown();
        }
        setup();
        function addDropdown() {
          var ctrl = L.control({position: 'topright'});
          ctrl.onAdd = function() {
            var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'info legend');
            div.innerHTML = '<b>Colour by</b><br><select style=\"margin-top:4px;\">' +
              data.vars.map(function(v) {
                return '<option value=\"' + v + '\">' + v + '</option>';
              }).join('') + '</select>';
            div.querySelector('select').addEventListener('change', function() {
              colourBy(this.value);
            });
            L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
            L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
            return div;
          };
          ctrl.addTo(map);
          colourBy(data.vars[0]);
        }
      }", data = list(vars = vars, cols = point_colours, n = n_fix))
}

# choose a flight segment - here the one closest to n locations
# (replace flight_n_explore with any other flight_n to explore a different flight)
flight_counts <- eagle_data %>% count(flight_n)
flight_n_explore <- flight_counts$flight_n[which.min(abs(flight_counts$n - 1500))]

segment_explore <- eagle_data %>% filter(flight_n == flight_n_explore)

flight_explorer(segment_explore, explore_vars, diverging = diverging_vars)

```

# Select the clustering variables 

We will pull out the same variables used in @Bergen2022-rj, and scale them to have mean = 0 and sd = 1.

```{r}

ready_to_cluster <- eagle_data %>%
  select(
    # F_AOG_sqrt,
    F_radians_abs_sqrt, 
    F_Sn_sqrt, 
    # F_speed_sqrt,
    F_Vrate, 
    # F_Vrate_abs
    ) %>%
  scale()

suppressWarnings(
  multi.hist(ready_to_cluster, global = FALSE, breaks=60,density=FALSE)
)

```

## Plot the correlation between the covariates

```{r}

ready_to_cluster %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  cor() %>% 
  corrplot::corrplot(method = "number", type = "upper", tl.col = "black")

```

The Sn and speed variables are highly correlated, but we will keep both for now as they are both used in the @Bergen2022-rj paper.

# K-means clustering

Will investigate for K in (2:7) as in paper. 10 random starting centroids each time. Increase iter.max to 30 to ensure algorithm has enough time to converge

```{r}

#Set seed to ensure the same labels get applied to the clusters each time it's run.
#If not set, will get same convergence but the labels will be shuffled
#(due to different initial randomly allocated cluster membership)
set.seed(234) 
k2 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 2, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

set.seed(234) 
k3 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 3, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

set.seed(234) 
k4 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 4, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

set.seed(234) 
k5 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 5, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

set.seed(234) 
k6 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 6, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

set.seed(234) 
k7 <- kmeans(ready_to_cluster, centers = 7, nstart = 10, iter.max = 30)

```



```{r}

#May throw warning message that it took many iterations to converge;
#should be okay as long as ifault = 0
k2$ifault
k3$ifault
k4$ifault
k5$ifault
k6$ifault
k7$ifault

```

## Choosing k

Next, we'll do some plotting to help us choose K.

### Within-sum-of-squares plot

```{r}

wss_df = data.frame(k = 2:7, 
                    wss = c(k2$tot.withinss,
                            k3$tot.withinss,
                            k4$tot.withinss,
                            k5$tot.withinss,
                            k6$tot.withinss,
                            k7$tot.withinss))

#Looking for an elbow, in order to determine "best k":
with(wss_df, plot(k,wss,type='b'))

#no obvious elbow.  

```

### Bootstrap the average silhouette width

Calculate the average silhouettes for B=100 bootstrap samples of size 1000 each (for computational ease). In paper, B = 1000 of size 10,000 each.

```{r}

B <- 100
avg.sils <- matrix(NA,B,6)
set.seed(992021)
for(b in 1:B){
  ids <- sample(1:nrow(ready_to_cluster),1000,replace=TRUE) 
  distmat <- dist(ready_to_cluster[ids,])
  clusters <- list(k2$cluster[ids],
                   k3$cluster[ids],
                   k4$cluster[ids],
                   k5$cluster[ids],
                   k6$cluster[ids],
                   k7$cluster[ids])
  for(i in 1:6) {
    sil <- silhouette(clusters[[i]],distmat) 
    avg.sils[b,i] <- mean(sil[,3])
  }
}

```



```{r}

plot(2:7, 
     avg.sils[1,],
     type='b',
     col='#00000040', 
     ylab='Average silhouette width', xlab = 'K',
     ylim=c(0.22,0.35)
     )

for(i in 2:nrow(avg.sils)) lines(2:7, avg.sils[i,],type='b',col='#00000040')

```

## Assign the cluster labels to the data

We also save the behaviour of each cluster of the 3-cluster model in a `behavior` column, so that the other scripts (such as `classification_agreement.qmd` and `energy_harvesting_data_prep.qmd`) don't need to label the clusters themselves. The behaviours are identified from the plots in [Assessing clusters](#assessing-clusters) below. The cluster numbers are arbitrary and can change when the data (e.g. a different eagle) or the variables change, so check that these labels still match those plots whenever the script is re-run.

```{r}

eagle_data <- eagle_data %>%
  mutate(k2 = k2$cluster,
         k3 = k3$cluster,
         k4 = k4$cluster,
         k5 = k5$cluster,
         k6 = k6$cluster,
         k7 = k7$cluster)

# the behaviour of each cluster of the 3-cluster model (see 'Assessing clusters' below)
state_1 <- "gliding"
state_2 <- "flapping"
state_3 <- "ascending"

# the behaviour of each fix, from the 3-cluster model
eagle_data <- eagle_data %>%
  mutate(behavior = case_when(k3 == 1 ~ state_1,
                              k3 == 2 ~ state_2,
                              k3 == 3 ~ state_3))

table(eagle_data$k3, eagle_data$behavior)

```

## Plot the k-means clusters on the PCA biplot

```{r}
#| results: asis

k_means_labs <- c("k2", "k3", "k4", "k5", "k6", "k7")

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")

for(i in 1:length(k_means_labs)) {

  k_name <- paste0("K = ", i + 1)
  
  p <- ggplot(data = eagle_subset) + 
    geom_point(aes(x = pc1, y = pc2, col = factor(.data[[k]])),shape='.') +

    ggtitle(k_name) +

                            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.025, "npc"), type = "open"),
                            lwd = 1) +
    geom_text(data = as.data.frame(pca$loadings[,1:2]), aes(x = Comp.1*6.5, y =  Comp.2*6.5,
                            label = rownames(pca$loadings)))  +
    theme_bw()
  
  # one tab per model: heading first, then the plot
  cat("\n\n#### ", k_name, "\n\n")
  print(p)
  
}

cat("\n\n:::\n")
```

# Assessing clusters

## Relationships of the flight variables 

### K = 3 clusters

Note that the cluster labels are different from those in the @Bergen2022-rj paper, due to different starting points in the k-means as the data here is just a subset of the data in the paper. 

Also, we have tried to remove perching fixes beforehand (but some still may remain). We will therefore identify the other three behaviours (ascending, flapping, gliding).

The behaviour of each cluster is set in [Assign the cluster labels to the data](#assign-the-cluster-labels-to-the-data) above (`state_1`, `state_2` and `state_3`), and saved in the CSV. If the plots below show that a cluster has the wrong label, change it there and re-run the script.

```{r}

eagle_subset <- eagle_subset %>%
  # reorder the levels
  mutate(behavior = factor(behavior, levels = c('ascending','flapping','gliding')))

```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Altitude above ground

We remove outliers for clarity and faster plotting.

```{r}

ggplot(data = eagle_subset) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = behavior, fill = behavior, y = F_AOG), outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) + 
  ylim(0, 1000) +
  labs(x = "Behavior", y = "Altitude above ground (m)") +
  theme_bw()

```

## Absolute turn angle

```{r}

# it looks like Silas didn't actually use Radians. He used absolute turn angle (create this column and plot)
eagle_subset$abs_angle = abs(eagle_subset$step_ta)

ggplot(data = eagle_subset) + 
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = behavior, fill = behavior, y = abs_angle), outlier.shape = NA) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values =cbpal[c(1,2,4,5)]) +

  theme_bw()

```

# Plotting flight paths

Find a relatively long one, but not so long that it's hard to see the colors.

```{r}

flight_lengths <- eagle_subset %>% 
  group_by(flight_n) %>% 
  summarize(len = n()) %>% 
  arrange(-len) 

# find the closest to n locations
flight_n_plot <- flight_lengths$flight_n[which.min(abs(flight_lengths$len - 1500))]

segment_to_plot <- eagle_subset %>%
```

# Data explorer with states

The same data explorer as above but this time also coloured by states (behaviours) identified by the k-means clustering.

```{r}

# the variables plotted in the previous chunks
explore_vars <- c("F_AOG", "F_radians", "F_speed", "F_Sn", "F_Vrate", "F_Vrate_abs", "F_radians_abs", "k3")

# variables with negative and positive values get a diverging palette centred on 0
diverging_vars <- c("F_radians", "F_Vrate")

# written as a function so it can be re-used later, e.g. with the k-means
# behaviour labels: flight_explorer(segment_to_plot, c("behavior", explore_vars))
flight_explorer <- function(segment, vars, diverging = character(0), height = 650) {

  segment <- segment %>% arrange(stepend_dtime)
  n_fix <- nrow(segment)

  # hover labels - timestamp and the (unclipped) value of every variable
  label_rows <- map(vars, \(v) {
    val <- segment[[v]]
    val <- if (is.numeric(val)) as.character(round(val, 3)) else as.character(val)
    paste0("<tr><td>", v, "</td>",
           "<td style='text-align:right; padding-left:10px;'><b>", val, "</b></td></tr>")
  })
  labels <- paste0("<b>", format(segment$stepend_dtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "</b>",
                   " (fix ", seq_len(n_fix), " of ", n_fix, ")",
                   "<table>", reduce(label_rows, paste0), "</table>") %>%
    map(htmltools::HTML)

  # colour palette for each variable
  make_palette <- function(x, v) {
    if (!is.numeric(x)) {
      okabe_ito <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
                     "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#999999")
      x <- factor(x)
      pal <- colorFactor(okabe_ito[seq_along(levels(x))], domain = x)
      return(list(pal = pal, x = x))
    }
    lims <- quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    if (v %in% diverging) {
      lims <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(lims))
      pal <- colorNumeric("RdBu", domain = lims, reverse = TRUE)
    } else {
      pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = lims)
    }
    list(pal = pal, x = pmin(pmax(x, lims[1]), lims[2])) # clip to the colour range
  }

  palettes <- map(set_names(vars), \(v) make_palette(segment[[v]], v))
  # the point colours for each variable (switched in the browser by the dropdown)
  point_colours <- map(palettes, \(p) p$pal(p$x))

  # a single layer of points (so the hover labels aren't duplicated for every variable)
  m <- leaflet(segment, height = height, width = "100%",
               options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
    addPolylines(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, color = "white", weight = 1,
                 opacity = 0.6, group = "Flight path") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat, radius = 4, stroke = FALSE,
                     fillColor = point_colours[[1]], fillOpacity = 0.9,
                     layerId = paste0("fix", seq_len(n_fix)), label = labels,
                     labelOptions = labelOptions(textsize = "12px", direction = "auto"))

  # one legend per variable - only the selected one is shown
  for (v in vars) {
    m <- m %>%
      addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = palettes[[v]]$pal, values = palettes[[v]]$x,
                title = v, opacity = 1, className = paste0("info legend legend-var legend-", v))
  }

  m %>%
    addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Flight path",
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
    addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>%
    # add a 'Colour by' dropdown that recolours the points and switches the legend
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var map = this;
        function colourBy(v) {
          var cols = data.cols[v];
          for (var i = 1; i <= data.n; i++) {
            var m = map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix' + i);
            if (m) m.setStyle({fillColor: cols[i - 1]});
          }
          el.querySelectorAll('.legend-var').forEach(function(l) {
            l.style.display = l.classList.contains('legend-' + v) ? '' : 'none';
          });
        }
        // leaflet only draws the layers once the map is visible (e.g. inside
        // a tab), so wait until the points exist before adding the dropdown
        function setup() {
          if (!map.layerManager || !map.layerManager.getLayer('marker', 'fix1')) {
            setTimeout(setup, 200);
            return;
          }
          addDropdown();
        }
        setup();
        function addDropdown() {
          var ctrl = L.control({position: 'topright'});
          ctrl.onAdd = function() {
            var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'info legend');
            div.innerHTML = '<b>Colour by</b><br><select style=\"margin-top:4px;\">' +
              data.vars.map(function(v) {
                return '<option value=\"' + v + '\">' + v + '</option>';
              }).join('') + '</select>';
            div.querySelector('select').addEventListener('change', function() {
              colourBy(this.value);
            });
            L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
            L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
            return div;
          };
          ctrl.addTo(map);
          colourBy(data.vars[0]);
        }
      }", data = list(vars = vars, cols = point_colours, n = n_fix))
}

# choose a flight segment - here the one closest to n locations
# (replace flight_n_explore with any other flight_n to explore a different flight)
flight_counts <- eagle_data %>% count(flight_n)
flight_n_explore <- flight_counts$flight_n[which.min(abs(flight_counts$n - 1500))]

segment_explore <- eagle_data %>% filter(flight_n == flight_n_explore)

flight_explorer(segment_explore, explore_vars, diverging = diverging_vars)

```

# Transition probabilities

```{r}

# create a data frame with the k3 cluster labels and flight_n to get transition probabilities between behaviours
transition_data = NULL
transition_data$k3 = eagle_data$k3
transition_data = as.data.frame(transition_data)
transition_data$flight_n = eagle_data$flight_n

# get a unique value for each segment end
transition_data = transition_data %>%
  group_by(flight_n) %>%
  mutate(segment_end = c(flight_n[-n()], paste("segment end")))

# get behavioural transitions
transition_data = transition_data %>% 
  mutate(old = case_when(
    k3==1~state_1,
    k3==2~state_2,
    k3==3~state_3)) %>% 
  # reorder the levels
  mutate(old = factor(old, levels = c('ascending','flapping','gliding')))

# get the state at the next location
transition_data = transition_data %>%
  mutate(new = lead(old))

# add a 'segment_end' label to the new column for the last fix in each flight segment
transition_data$new2 = ifelse(transition_data$segment_end == "segment end",'segment end',paste(transition_data$new))

# only interested in transitions to a different behaviour - so remove all rows with transitions to same behaviour
# transition_data = transition_data[transition_data$old != transition_data$new2,]
transMat = prop.table(with(transition_data, table(old, new2)), 1)
as.data.frame(transMat)

```

## Plot a transition matrix

```{r}

trans_df <- as.data.frame(transMat)

trans_df$new2 <- factor(trans_df$new2,
                        levels = c('ascending','flapping','gliding','segment end'))

ggplot(trans_df, aes(x = new2, y = old, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Freq, 2)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue", limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +   # first state at the top, like a matrix
  labs(x = "Next behaviour", y = "Current behaviour",
       fill = "Probability",
       title = "Behavioural transition probabilities") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

```

## Season

```{r}

## Season ##
# Season column
# seasonplotdat = plotdat[plotdat$name == "Floki" | plotdat$name == "Ernie" | plotdat$name == "Maxie" ,]

getSeason <- function(DATES) {
    WS <- as.Date("2012-6-21", format = "%Y-%m-%d",tz = "Australia/Hobart") # Winter Solstice
    SE <- as.Date("2012-9-23",  format = "%Y-%m-%d",tz = "Australia/Hobart") # Spring Equinox
    SS <- as.Date("2012-12-21",  format = "%Y-%m-%d",tz = "Australia/Hobart") # Summer Solstice
    FE <- as.Date("2012-3-21",  format = "%Y-%m-%d",tz = "Australia/Hobart") # Fall Equinox
    # Convert dates from any year to 2012 dates
    d <- as.Date(strftime(DATES, format="2012-%m-%d",tz = "Australia/Hobart"))
    ifelse (d >= WS & d < SE, "Winter",
      ifelse (d >= SE & d < SS, "Spring",
        ifelse (d >= SS | d < FE, "Summer", "Autumn")))
}

eagle_data$season = getSeason(eagle_data$date)
# create these labels for adding total percent of data to plots
labs = eagle_data %>%
  count(season) %>%
  mutate(
    perc = round(proportions(n) * 100, 1),
    cyl = as.factor(season)
    )

  scale_fill_manual(values = cbpal[c(2,4,5)]) +
```
